solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Perseverance in row as Egypt undergoes change

indicators.note: the letters of the words before this phrase are altered into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A rowing crew needs grit as it watches Egypt transform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undergoes change' rearranges IN ROW AS EGYPT, all twelve letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Perseverance is the stamina to keep going, a synonym for endurance.

clue.text: Drunk present? That'll teach you!

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard
here means in attendance, present

explanation.surface: Someone scolds a tipsy guest who has turned up.
explanation.definitionFit: A taunting exclamation of triumph, used idiomatically when someone gets their comeuppance.

clue.text: A communist protects last of them with weapons

indicators.note: one word guarding another means it surrounds it

parts.note: red is a standard label for a communist

indicators.note: the final letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A communist bodyguard shields the last of a group with guns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protects' puts M, the last of 'them', inside RED.
explanation.definitionFit: Being armed means carrying or equipped with weapons, an adjectival synonym.

clue.text: Hospital and home unshakeable on a case of remedy

parts.note: in means at home
firm means steady, not to be shaken

indicators.note: the outer letters of the next word form its case

explanation.surface: A hospital and a sturdy home are found on a medicine pack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' takes the outside letters R and Y of 'remedy'.
explanation.definitionFit: An infirmary is a place for treating the sick, often a hospital's name.

clue.text: Happy, having gone without one young man!

indicators.note: one word being without another means those letters are taken away

parts.note: taken as the word itself
a lad is a boy or young man

explanation.surface: Someone is cheerful now that a certain young suitor has left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes ONE from GONE, leaving G.
explanation.definitionFit: Glad and happy are direct synonyms for being pleased.

clue.text: Manage to catch some cricket and try

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls in cricket, a portion of the game
to hear a case is to try it in court

explanation.surface: Someone describes a passage of cricket followed by a rugby try.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an OVER is six balls from one bowler; 'try' is the legal sense, as a judge hears a case.
explanation.definitionFit: To overhear is to pick up speech accidentally, catching what was not meant for you.

clue.text: Spot a reporter holding up source of inspiration

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters read from bottom to top
the phrase holds the letters within it, spanning the words

explanation.surface: A journalist is spotted carrying something up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' finds OTARE inside 'Spot a reporter'; 'up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is one of the nine Muses, of lyric and love poetry, so a source of inspiration.

clue.text: Portugal involved in distribution of opiates — how suitable!

indicators.note: one item is wrapped up within another
the letters of the drug name are dealt out in a new order

parts.note: P is the international vehicle code for Portugal

explanation.surface: Portugal is implicated in a drug-trafficking network, a fitting scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distribution of' rearranges OPIATES; 'involved in' puts P inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: Apposite means fitting or appropriate to the circumstances, so an exclamation of aptness.

clue.text: Go and live with a fool without women

parts.note: to be is to exist or live

indicators.note: the letter for women is dropped from the word before

parts.note: a twit is a silly person

explanation.surface: Someone sets up home with a foolish partner in a household of men.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' drops W from TWIT, leaving TIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Beat it is a slang command to leave immediately, meaning clear off.

clue.text: Limited period for structure after backing issue

indicators.note: the structure word comes after the turned piece
going backwards means the following word is read in reverse

parts.note: to emit is to give out or issue
a frame is a supporting structure

explanation.surface: A deadline is set for a building once the publication is supported.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses the issue word, and 'after' signals that the structure word follows it, so the clue's order is reversed in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A timeframe is the span of time allotted for something to happen.

clue.text: King George takes no part in struggle for fruit

indicators.note: the monarch's letters drop out of the word for struggle

parts.note: to grapple is to wrestle or struggle
GR stands for Georgius Rex, King George

explanation.surface: A monarch declines to join a tussle over some fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: GR is the royal cipher for Georgius Rex, King George.
explanation.definitionFit: An apple is a common orchard fruit.

clue.text: Stand close, anticipating river

indicators.note: coming before, so the close word precedes the river

parts.note: an end is the close of something
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: Someone stays near the water ahead of a river crossing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ure is a river in North Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand something is to bear or tolerate it, a synonym.

clue.text: Go away and sell tickets for fight to the death

parts.note: shoo is a command telling something to go away
to tout is to sell tickets at inflated prices

explanation.surface: A ticket seller is told to clear off before a deadly fight.
explanation.walkthrough: A tout in Britain is a ticket scalper.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoot-out is a decisive gunfight, often ending in death.

clue.text: Obstruction in the way of listener

definitions.text: Obstruction in the way of listener

parts.words: Obstruction in the way of listener
parts.note: read as a blockage in a hearing organ rather than someone standing in a listener's path

explanation.definitionFit: Waxy secretion in the auditory canal can block hearing, a playful description.

clue.text: Family member engineers crucial uprising with energy

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means the word reads upwards

parts.note: vital means crucial
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A relative in the military engineers sparks a vital rebellion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' turns VITAL into LATIV. RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: A relative is a person connected by blood or marriage, someone in your family.

clue.text: Renovation of key service elevator?

parts.note: F is a musical key
an ace is an unreturnable serve in tennis
lift is the British word for elevator

explanation.surface: Someone asks for the main service lift to be repaired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' is the tennis sense, a serve.
explanation.definitionFit: A facelift is figuratively a renovation that smartens a building's appearance.

clue.text: Passing macho types mainly accepted by pearl divers

indicators.note: something accepted is taken inside another
divers means various or assorted, so the letters are rearranged
most of the word, losing its last letter

parts.note: he-men are macho types

explanation.surface: Tough guys are briefly taken on by pearl-fishing divers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divers' is the old adjective meaning several, not people who dive; 'mainly' trims the last letter, and 'accepted by' puts the trimmed piece inside the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemeral means short-lived or fleeting, things that are passing.

clue.text: Declines to accept arrest of aspirants

indicators.note: taking something in, so one word encloses another

parts.note: wanes means declines or fades
to nab is to arrest

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to accept the arrest of hopefuls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Declines' looks like a verb meaning refuses, but it is a synonym for fading; 'to accept' places the arrest word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Wannabes are people aspiring to fame or a role they want to have.

clue.text: Total staff for chap taking weekly payments

parts.note: a tally is a running total
to man is to staff

explanation.surface: Someone totals up staff numbers for a debt collector.
explanation.walkthrough: A tallyman in Britain sold goods on credit and called weekly to collect payments.
explanation.definitionFit: A tallyman is a collector who calls round for instalment payments.

clue.text: Rang out, being instructed in broadcast

indicators.note: something said on air is heard, giving its sound

parts.note: told means instructed

explanation.surface: Bells ring out after being commanded on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolled means a bell sounded slowly and repeatedly, so it rang out.

clue.text: Casts off, carrying king in rags …

indicators.note: one word carries the other inside

parts.note: sheds means casts off
R is short for rex, king

explanation.surface: Someone discards clothing and carries a king who wears tatters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' puts R inside SHEDS.
explanation.definitionFit: Shreds are torn strips of cloth, a synonym for rags.

clue.text: Doubtful if stays are enough

definitions.note: plural verb phrase, matching the infinitive in sense of being enough

indicators.note: uncertain, so the letters are arranged unsettledly

explanation.surface: Someone doubts whether corsets will suffice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doubtful' rearranges IF STAYS. Stays are corsets.
explanation.definitionFit: To satisfy a requirement is to meet it, being sufficient.

clue.text: … not to mention being terribly late and solitary

indicators.note: badly, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: lone means solitary

explanation.surface: Someone is tardy and alone, and nobody mentions it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges LATE to LETA.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning much less or still less, used like 'never mind'.

clue.text: Light source of labour when editor evacuated

indicators.note: the first letter of labour is its source

parts.note: as means when

indicators.note: emptied, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: A light source powers the work after the editor leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'source of' takes L; 'evacuated' leaves E and R from 'editor'.
explanation.definitionFit: A laser emits an intense beam, making it a source of light.

clue.text: Give one million — and some

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
part means some

explanation.surface: Someone offers one million plus a bit more.
explanation.definitionFit: To impart is to give or convey.

clue.text: A couple of names — that is another one

indicators.note: a couple means two, so the abbreviation for the following word is written twice over

parts.note: N stands for name
i.e. is short for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A list of two names leads to one more.
explanation.definitionFit: Annie is a girl's name, so another of the names mentioned.

clue.text: Journal left in loo?

indicators.note: one letter goes inside the word for loo

parts.note: bog is British slang for loo

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a diary in the toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: Bog is British slang for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: A blog is an online journal of posts.

clue.text: Star working villages without delay

indicators.note: in operation, so the letters are reworked
the delay word is removed from villages

parts.note: lag means delay

explanation.surface: A celebrity is touring villages without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes LAG from VILLAGES to leave VILES; 'working' rearranges that.
explanation.definitionFit: Elvis Presley was a famous singing star.

clue.text: Investor calls for entertainment venues in Spain

parts.note: a bull is an investor expecting prices to rise
rings means calls on the phone

explanation.surface: An investor phones about places of entertainment in Spain.
explanation.definitionFit: Bullrings are arenas for bullfighting, a traditional Spanish spectacle.

clue.text: Allergy developed by force in designated area of Parliament

parts.note: to press is to force

indicators.note: changed in form, so the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An allergy flared up in a restricted part of Parliament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges ALLERGY.
explanation.definitionFit: The press gallery is the section in the House reserved for journalists.
